newsitem.title: INDIA: India eases import procedures to cut customs time.
newsitem.headline: India eases import procedures to cut customs time.

text.p: The Indian government said on Friday it had simplified import procedures by allowing importers to file their documents for clearance by customs authorities 30 days before the arrival of the goods.

"Importers can also present their documents against cargo coming in mother vessels bringing goods from the port of loading to intermediate ports without waiting for the details of the feeder vessel which ultimately brings goods into the Indian port," the Finance Ministry said in a statement.
The statement said documents will be assessed in advance so that importers can pay their customs duties and get their goods cleared immediately on their arrival.

"This has been done to reduce the time taken in clearance of goods, resulting in a reduction in the amount paid to foreign shipping companies in foreign exchange as container detention charges, ports demurrage charges (and) interest on capital involved,..." it said.
The move would also ease port congestion, the statement added.
